Let me see if I can clear it up.

CELL is name of the processor architecture developed by IBM, it was only used in a handful of devices. x86 and x64 architectures were developed by AMD/Intel and are the type of processor architectures that are in 99% of desktops and laptops.

Programs and operating systems are built such that they rely on a specific instruction sets (you can think of them as tools) which are unique to architectures (think of them as tool boxes) which means programs (think of them as products created using a set of tools) can only work on CPU architectures that support the necessary instruction sets.

All microchips made of transistors have a production size standard, otherwise called a node. You can think of transistors like LEGO blocks that are used to make microchips, all the blocks have a particular size and shape, structures made of those blocks have to have their designs built around the size constraints those blocks allow.

As tech has progressed chip foundries (LEGO block makers) have found ways to shrink the size of the LEGO blocks which allows more blocks to be put in to the same amount of space and a more complex design be implemented.

The problem is that these foundries have to rework their production machines such that they make only the new smaller sized LEGO blocks, meaning that structures that had their designs based on the older larger LEGO blocks can no longer be built unless those structures are redesigned to use the new smaller blocks, this costs time and money.

What that means is that it's often cheaper to move to a new design that uses a more current node than it is to maintain an older design that uses older production technology. Or in other words it was cheaper for Sony to move to the PS4 than it was to keep making PS3's.
